t: The Alaska Railroad Revolving Fund shall continue available until expended for the work authorized by law, including operation and maintenance of oceangoing or coastwise vessels by ownership, charter, or arrangement with other branches of the Government service, for the purpose of providing additional facilities for transportation of freight, passenger, or mail, when deemed necessary for the benefit and development of industries or travel in the area served and payment of compensation and expenses as authorized by 5 U.S.C. 8146, to be reimbursed as therein provided: Provided, That no employee shall be paid an annual salary out of said fund in excess of the salaries prescribed by the Classification Act of 1949, as amended, for grade GS–15, except the general manager of said railroad, one assistant general manager at not to exceed the salaries prescribed by said Act for GS–17, and five officers at not to exceed the salaries prescribed by said Act for grade GS–16.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision keeping the Alaska Railroad Revolving Fund available for authorized work and capping employee salaries. The tempting reading is that an "arrangement with other branches of the Government service" is coordination, but that stays entirely inside the federal government. Nothing in the section provides for consultation, hearings, comment, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue involving any outside party.
fable.s: by ownership, charter, or arrangement with other branches of the Government service

opus.w: This section only says the Alaska Railroad Revolving Fund stays available and limits the salaries paid from it. The only coordination it mentions is 'arrangement with other branches of the Government service.' That is coordination inside the federal government, so it does not count as participation. No outside party is consulted, and there is no public hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue.
opus.s: including operation and maintenance of oceangoing or coastwise vessels by ownership, charter, or arrangement with other branches of the Government service
opus.b: The section is an appropriations-style provision. The tempting reading is that "arrangement with other branches of the Government service" signals participation. It doesn't, because that coordination happens entirely inside the federal government. Nothing in the section brings in states, the public, experts or companies, and there is no hearing, comment period or rulemaking.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the use of funds for operations and maintenance, including arrangements with other federal government branches. It does not require consultation or coordination with any parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, or the public). The mention of 'other branches of the Government service' refers to intra-governmental coordination, which is explicitly excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: The Alaska Railroad Revolving Fund shall continue available until expended for the work authorized by law, including operation and maintenance of oceangoing or coastwise vessels by ownership, charter, or arrangement with other branches of the Government service
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "arrangement with other branches of the Government service" implies coordination with outside entities. However, "branches of the Government service" refers to other federal agencies or departments, which are inside the federal government. Furthermore, the text primarily concerns appropriations and salary limits for federal employees. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or private entities before making a decision.
